title: Prayer times in the far north
word: Prayer times in the far north
hookLine: where the sun barely sets, scholars give rulings for prayer and fasting

lines: A TABLE SET, A SKY STILL BRIGHT.
cards: Midsummer, somewhere far north. It's late in the evening and the sky is still bright. A family has been fasting since before dawn, and dawn came early, because night never quite arrived.
The table is set. The dates are out. Someone keeps checking the window.
The sun touches the horizon, slides along it, and seems unwilling to go. When the Qur'an says fast until night, and the night barely comes, what do you do?

teach.h: DAWN AND NIGHTFALL SET THE FAST.
teach.b: The Qur'an ties the fast to the sky.

In Pickthall's translation, the believers may "eat and drink until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn. Then strictly observe the fast till nightfall." Dawn and nightfall.

The daily prayers are tied to the sun's movements the same way. In Mecca and Medina, the sun keeps steady hours. Far north, in summer, the dawn light may never fully fade, and in winter the day may hardly come.
Scholars turn to a report in Sahih Muslim.

teach.h: A DAY AS LONG AS A YEAR.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, spoke of a time to come when a day would be as long as a year. His companions asked the obvious question: will one day's prayers be enough for that day?
He said no; estimate its measure, and pray accordingly. So the principle is already there: when the sun stops being a usable clock, you measure. How to measure is where the views differ.

teach.h: NEAREST PLACE, MECCA, OR YOUR OWN SKY.
teach.b: Some scholars say to follow the times of the nearest place where day and night are still clearly distinct. Some say to follow the times of Mecca.
Some say that if the long fast can be kept, keep it by your own sky, and estimate only when the signs disappear or the strain becomes too great.
Behind all of them stands a line from the close of the same chapter, in Pickthall's words: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." The family at the window isn't facing a gap in their religion.
They're standing where a question was already asked and answered.

how: Muslims living far north follow rulings from scholars and local councils: some pray and fast by the times of the nearest place with a clear day and night, some by the times of Mecca, and some by their own sky when the signs can still be seen.

games.q: what does “prayer times in the far north” mean?
o: the custom of praying only while the sun is fully up
times estimated where the sun barely sets or barely rises
a rule excusing people near the poles from prayer and fasting

games.q: the far north — tap the pairs.
p: a day as long as a year
not a soul beyond its scope
the close of the chapter of the fast

s: the sources never imagined a day without normal hours
a report in Sahih Muslim speaks of a day as long as a year, and the answer: estimate its measure.
scholars give one single ruling for the far north
some follow the nearest place with clear day and night, some Mecca, some the local sky when it can be read.
the Qur'an says no soul is tasked beyond its scope
"Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope" (2:286, Pickthall).

games.q: you're one of the companions. the Prophet has just described a day as long as a year. you ask: will one day's prayers be enough for it? what does he answer?
o: yes, the usual prayers once for the whole long day.
no; estimate its measure and pray accordingly.
no prayer is due until normal days return.
games.why: no: estimate its measure. some scholars working on prayer times near the poles start from this answer.

practice: Picture that kitchen far north, light still at the window late at night, the table waiting, and then someone there on a winter morning, praying in the dark before a sun that will barely rise.
Hold them both for a few breaths, under a sky that won't cooperate. If you pray, keep them in your prayers; if you don't, let your own sky feel a little more ordinary, and a little more of a gift.

wordCard.voice: Prayer times in the far north. Where the sun barely sets or barely rises, scholars estimate the times for prayer and fasting. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: capacity or scope; 2:286 says no soul is tasked beyond it.

carryVoice: Your line: ramadan under the midnight sun. Estimate its measure; no soul is tasked beyond its scope. Rest well.
